name: Ripple-65B Preview (BF16, NVFP4, Base, DFlash2)

lineage.base_model: pretrained from scratch (12T tokens; recipe started from an Olmo 3 baseline)
lineage.how_derived: midtrain 200B, long context, SFT, LC SFT and mixed-domain RL; light post-training focused on agentic coding (card)

purpose: Strong agentic coding and reasoning from a dense 65B model that fits consumer hardware such as an NVIDIA DGX Spark; the builder chose a modernised dense transformer instead of an MoE to reduce training and infrastructure complexity (card).

license.name: Apache-2.0
license.notes: Card header links an Apache 2.0 LICENSE file that exists in the repo (not read).

architecture.kind: dense transformer, 65B, 80 layers, d_model 5120 (thin-and-deep), Gemma-3N-like layout with overprovisioned attention heads, high sliding-window-to-global ratio and small SWA window, FFN activation clipping, gated attention, global NoPE, value residuals
architecture.attention: sliding window plus global NoPE layers
architecture.why_this_design: Builder: simple sharding without custom kernels at 40% MFU, thin-and-deep aspect ratio and Gemma-3N-style changes for stability and reasoning at scale (card).

variants.notes: instruction-tuned; repo total per HF API

pc-12gb.variant: GGUF Q4_K_M 40.43 GB (dense: decode bound by RAM bandwidth for the part outside VRAM)
pc-12gb.notes: 40.4 GB file against 9.6 GB VRAM plus 50 GB RAM budget; part streams from RAM (dense: decode is bandwidth bound)

pc-16gb.variant: GGUF Q4_K_M 40.43 GB (dense: decode bound by RAM bandwidth for the part outside VRAM)
pc-16gb.notes: 40.4 GB file against 13.6 GB VRAM plus 50 GB RAM budget; part streams from RAM (dense: decode is bandwidth bound)

pc-24gb.variant: GGUF Q4_K_M 40.43 GB (dense: decode bound by RAM bandwidth for the part outside VRAM)
pc-24gb.notes: 40.4 GB file against 21.6 GB VRAM plus 82 GB RAM budget; part streams from RAM (dense: decode is bandwidth bound)

pc-32gb.variant: GGUF Q4_K_M 40.43 GB (dense: decode bound by RAM bandwidth for the part outside VRAM)
pc-32gb.notes: 40.4 GB file against 29.6 GB VRAM plus 114 GB RAM budget; part streams from RAM (dense: decode is bandwidth bound)

mac-16-24gb.variant: GGUF Q4_K_M 40.43 GB (dense: decode bound by RAM bandwidth for the part outside VRAM)
mac-16-24gb.notes: 40.4 GB file against a GPU share of about 12 GB (KV cache not included)

mac-32gb.variant: GGUF Q4_K_M 40.43 GB (dense: decode bound by RAM bandwidth for the part outside VRAM)
mac-32gb.notes: 40.4 GB file against a GPU share of about 22 GB (KV cache not included)

mac-64gb+.variant: GGUF Q4_K_M 40.43 GB (dense: decode bound by RAM bandwidth for the part outside VRAM)
mac-64gb+.notes: 40.4 GB file against a GPU share of about 52 GB (KV cache not included)

other: vLLM (day-0 'ripple' reasoning and tool parsers, v0.34.0)
engine_support.notes: A llama.cpp arch for Ripple was not found in the b11042-b12549 release titles; the community GGUFs imply support or a fork, unchecked.

benchmarks.name: Terminal-Bench 2.1
benchmarks.variant: instruct BF16, OpenCode harness unless stated
benchmarks.harness: card table vs Reflection Beam 501B 80.1, Muse Spark Open 816B 76.4, Inkling 975B 63.8, Nemotron 3 Ultra 550B 56.4; some comparison scores are the vendor's own re-runs (italics in the card)

strengths: dense 65B that quantizes to 18-40 GB with large vendor-reported agentic coding scores
weaknesses: dense: slow decode when not fully in VRAM
soft.maturity: New lab (team of 1 to 5 people during development per card); 616 likes within two weeks.

tona_fit.reason: A dense 65B coding/agent model whose Q3-Q4 GGUFs (28-40 GB) suit the 32 GB class with some RAM and the 64 GB+ Macs; the vendor's Terminal-Bench 2.1 of 80.5 is a claim to reproduce with our own harness (eval checklist) before any offer. Dense 65B decode is bandwidth bound.
